# PEN-2585 — point `AGENT_HOME` at a path the pod actually mounts

PR: _(filed from PEN-2585; see the issue for the measurement trail)_

## Files

- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.agent-home.test.ts` (new)

## What changed

`buildEnvVars` previously projected `AGENT_HOME` straight from
`workspaceContext.agentHome`. The server computes that as
`resolveDefaultAgentWorkspaceDir(agent.id)` = `<instanceRoot>/workspaces/<agentId>`
and `mkdir -p`s it on **its own** `/paperclip` mount before handing it over.

The pod mounts no such path. Measured 2026-11-07 on the live Cto pod
(`claude_k8s`, external instructions bundle):

```
the exported agent-home path   ->  <instanceRoot>/workspaces/<agentId>  ->  ENOENT
ls /paperclip/instances/default                                         ->  data  skills
findmnt -T /paperclip/instances/default                                 ->  emptyDir instance-overlay
```

`instances/default` arrives as the 16 MiB `instance-overlay` emptyDir with `data/`
and `skills/` bound over it and **nothing** bound at `workspaces/`. So the variable
was set, pointed at an identically-spelled directory on a volume the pod does not
have, and every `$AGENT_HOME/...` read was ENOENT.

This is PEN-4932 invariant 9 — the failure `isWorkspaceLessFallbackWorkspaceDir`
already documents for the workspace cwd ("the server realizes every execution
workspace onto its OWN `/paperclip` mount … the pod's identically-spelled path
resolves to nothing") — reached through a second variable that nothing guards.

Now: for an `external` instructions bundle, `AGENT_HOME` resolves to
`instructionsRootPath`. That root is the per-seat CephFS directory on the
`paperclip-data` PVC, and this adapter **already** binds it into the pod via
`agentBundleRoot` → `resolveScopedWritableMounts` — so it is mounted, durable and
writable by construction, and it is where the charter's companions actually live.
`$AGENT_HOME/{HEARTBEAT,SOUL,TOOLS}.md` resolve for the first time. Any agent
without an external bundle keeps the previous value unchanged.

This is the fix `opencode_k8s` shipped at its own copy of this call site. Note its
comment there asserts *"claude_k8s agents (whose AGENT_HOME already IS the bundle
dir) worked"* — that premise is **false** and was never measured against this tree,
which is why the bug outlived the change that named it. The sibling comment is left
alone here; this entry is the correction of record.

The `AGENT_HOME` row in the env-classification table also claimed the value was
"on the mounted PVC" unqualified. True for the external-bundle case, false for the
fallback; the reason string now says which is which. Classification is unchanged
(`SAFE_LITERAL` — a filesystem path either way, never credential material).

## Why a manifest test

`job-manifest.agent-home.test.ts` asserts the env value **and** that a volumeMount
with that exact `mountPath` exists on the container that reads it. The half that
was missing all along is the join: an env var naming a durable-looking path proves
nothing on its own, which is exactly what shipped. A negative control pins that the
old server-side path is mounted nowhere, so the fallback branch is still understood
to be a fallback onto nothing for bundle-less agents.

## Blast radius

Env-only, one adapter, one variable. No manifest shape, mount set, PATH or
credential wiring changes. Agents without `instructionsBundleMode: "external"`
are byte-identical.
